football_evidence.question: Can Tulsa’s pass rush get to Army’s quarterback?
football_evidence.assessment: EdgeDesk’s number is 7.8 points closer to Army than the line, and EdgeDesk cannot account for most of that: its own breakdown accounts for about 0.0 of the 7.8 points. The measured football evidence leans toward Tulsa, not toward EdgeDesk’s number. Treat the gap as an open research question, not as an edge.

When Army has the ball (third down): Army’s offense converts 51.9% of its third downs, and Tulsa’s defense allows opponents to convert 40.6% of their third downs (FBS average 39.7%).
Dexter Williams II has completed 34 of 60 passes (56.7%) for 340 yards, 5.7 yards per attempt, 3 touchdowns and no interceptions in three games for Tulsa, and has been sacked on 3 of 63 dropbacks.
EdgeDesk’s position-group ratings put Army’s receivers No. 63 nationally and Tulsa’s No. 136.
contradicting: When Tulsa has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): Tulsa’s offense has allowed a sack on 3.9% of its dropbacks, and Army’s defense sacks the quarterback on 4.2% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.6%).
